question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund's strategy document says: 'We take long and short positions across currencies, fixed income, equities, commodities, real assets and interest rate derivatives based on macro-economic trend analysis.' This best matches which Cat III strategy?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10.1.2 defines Global-Macro as long/short across currencies, fixed income, equities, commodities, real assets and rates, driven by macro trends — the description is a verbatim fit. The Trap: Market-neutral stays within equity pairs; Convertible arb is single-issuer; Pre-IPO is private-to-public equity. None allow the multi-asset multi-geography scope of Global-Macro. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers Global-Macro similarly. VIII (Equity Derivatives) is narrower (equity only). XIX-D does NOT cover Global-Macro since Cat I/II cannot run this strategy. Manager's Pro-Tip: Global-Macro books often run 1.5-1.9x leverage (close to Cat III 2x cap) because single-trade Sharpe is modest; aggregate risk via VaR/CVaR at 99% confidence with 1-day horizon, and stress-test for correlated macro shocks (2008, 2013 taper, 2020 COVID).
